# PAROTITIS

Infection of salivary tissue is a relatively common disease. It is usually caused by a stone in the parotid duct, dehydration, or a viral infection. Sialolithiasis in elderly patients often leads to ductal obstruction and secondary infection. Other predisposing factors for ductal occlusion include dehydration, anticholinergic medications such as tricyclics and diphenhydramine, general disability and trauma. Once culture results are available adjust antimicrobial therapy based on specific etiologic organism.

[More information on Parotitis](more-about-parotitis)

## Duration of Therapy

Therapy duration varies based on clinical response to treatment and is typically 10-14 days.

## Viral Parotitis

Suspect mumps parotitis if there is fever, malaise, earache and bilateral tender swelling of the parotid glands. For mumps parotitis, treat with warm compresses, analgesics, and maintain good hydration to prevent secondary bacterial infection. Other viral causes of parotitis include influenza and enteroviruses.

Therapy:
## Immunocompetent Patient

Preferred:
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($) [M] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h ($) [DI]
< OR >
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($) [M] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg PO q8h ($) [DI]
< OR >
Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h ($) [R]

If MRSA suspected or alternative to above:
[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h ($) [DI]
< OR >
Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg PO q8h ($) [DI]
